items.prompt: Describe how a column of centimetre readings should be recorded when its instrument is read to one decimal place.
items.canonical_answer: Readings have one decimal place throughout, including trailing zeros such as 5.0 cm.
marking_guidance: Credit 1 (1): Consistent one decimal place including trailing zeros; instrument precision, not calculator digits.
Accept tenths of a centimetre recorded throughout, including 5.0 rather than 5 where appropriate.
Credit the requested action; unrelated procedural detail does not earn an extra mark.

items.prompt: Draw labelled axes suitable for times from 0 to 10 s and positions from 5 to 35 cm, using regular numerical intervals.
items.canonical_answer:
The horizontal axis is Time / s, spanning 0–10 with regular intervals. The vertical axis is Position / cm, covering 5–35 with a regular scale.

![Original graphical solution](assets/figure-6118-3-01.png)
marking_guidance: Credit 1 (1): Horizontal time scale regularly covering 0–10 s.
Credit 2 (1): Vertical position scale regularly covering 5–35 cm, with axis quantities/units; zero is not compulsory for position.

Maximum 2 marks. Accept equivalent scientifically correct wording or a labelled representation of the same points. Count each distinct idea once; an unsupported keyword alone is not a causal explanation.
Accept an equivalent correctly labelled graph or diagram; the requested scale, point placement, direction or gradient feature must remain clear.

items.prompt: Calculate the gradient of a straight temperature–time line through (10 s, 68 °C) and (50 s, 60 °C). Include the sign and unit.
items.canonical_answer: Gradient = (60 − 68)/(50 − 10). The result is −0.20 °C/s.
marking_guidance: 1 mark for difference in temperature divided by difference in time, using both coordinate pairs in matching order.
1 mark for −0.20 °C/s or −12 °C/min. A positive magnitude without the cooling sign is incomplete. Retain the method mark after arithmetic error; one-point y/x is invalid for this nonzero intercept.
Accept an equivalent equation and numerical substitution/working. The answer must use compatible units; apply the stated method and follow-through rules.

objective_titles: Calculate straight-line gradient as change in vertical quantity divided by change in horizontal quantity; retain sign and axis-ratio units.

items.prompt: Explain how repeated readings of 15.8, 15.8 and 15.9 cm can be precise but inaccurate if the accepted length is 15.0 cm.
items.canonical_answer: The readings agree closely, so their spread is small. Their common displacement above 15.0 cm shows poor accuracy despite that agreement.
marking_guidance: Credit 1 (1): Close agreement shows precision.
Credit 2 (1): Common displacement from accepted value shows poor accuracy; do not equate precision with truth.

items.prompt: Explain the link between random scatter and systematic offset when assessing a fitted graph.
items.canonical_answer: Random variation spreads observations around a trend. A systematic offset can shift the trend without necessarily producing much scatter.
marking_guidance: Credit 1 (1): Random errors spread points on either side.
Credit 2 (1): Systematic error shifts the trend consistently; either can occur without the other.

items.prompt:
Investigation aim: measure a model vehicle’s speed from position and time. These are invented, idealised practice readings; real readings have scatter. 

| Time / s | Position / cm |
|---:|---:|
| 0 | 5 |
| 2 | 11 |
| 4 | 17 |
| 6 | 23 |
| 8 | 29 |
| 10 | 35 |

(a) Draw Position / cm vertically against Time / s horizontally. Plot the supplied readings and add a separate fitted line. [5]
(b) Show two widely separated points on your fitted line and calculate its gradient. State the gradient unit. [3]
(c) Plan how to measure a model vehicle’s speed from position and time. Name the equipment and arrangement, describe the measurements and repeats, state controls and a relevant precaution, design the results table and explain how the results answer the aim. [8]
items.canonical_answer:
Graph: Position / cm is vertical and Time / s horizontal. Use the six readings, draw a separate best-fit line and show a wide gradient triangle; do not join scattered readings in a zigzag.

Gradient construction: choose the separated fitted-line points (0, 5) and (10, 35). Gradient = (35 − 5) / (10 − 0) = 3 cm/s. The slope is speed, 3 cm/s. The 5 cm position intercept does not change speed.

Arrangement: A low-speed trolley on a level track with a metre rule and a phone or camera recording the scale and a visible timer

Plan: 1. Set the camera square to a visible centimetre scale along the level track. 2. Record the trolley moving at a fixed low drive setting with the timer or frame rate known. 3. Choose a starting frame as t = 0 and record the trolley reference point position. 4. Read positions at 2 s intervals from the recording using the same reference point. 5. Repeat the run at the same setting and record the corresponding positions in repeat columns.
Control and accuracy: Keep the track arrangement, drive setting and starting position matched; reduce parallax by reading the scale consistently.
Table: Time / s; Position / cm; repeat readings in separate columns. 
Graph and conclusion: The slope is speed, 3 cm/s. The 5 cm position intercept does not change speed. Compare repeated readings and report the tested range rather than claiming an exact law from scattered observations.

![Original fitted practice graph](assets/practical-6118-3.png)
marking_guidance: (a) Correct quantities and units on both axes (1); regular usable scales (1); points within half a small square, all six (2) or four/five (1); a separate suitable fitted line (1).

(b) A visible wide triangle or two stated separated line coordinates (1); difference in vertical coordinates divided by difference in horizontal coordinates, with correct sign and result (1); unit cm/s or a stated equivalent derived from vertical unit / horizontal unit (1).
(c) Equipment/arrangement (1): A low-speed trolley on a level track with a metre rule and a phone or camera recording the scale and a visible timer

(c) Measurements (3): One mark each for: Record the trolley moving at a fixed low drive setting with the timer or frame rate known.; Read positions at 2 s intervals from the recording using the same reference point.; Repeat the run at the same setting and record the corresponding positions in repeat columns.

(c) Controls/precaution (2): one mark for a named variable AND how it is kept fixed; one for another specific control or a relevant precaution with its action. Keep the track arrangement, drive setting and starting position matched; reduce parallax by reading the scale consistently.
(c) Table (1): Time / s; Position / cm; repeat readings in separate columns.

(c) Analysis/conclusion (1): The slope is speed, 3 cm/s. The 5 cm position intercept does not change speed. Compare repeated readings and report the tested range rather than claiming an exact law from scattered observations.

Accept a physically equivalent operational method using suitable named equipment. Do not award a second graph-construction mark in (c). For later calculations, allow error carried forward from a plausible measured gradient when the subsequent relation is correct; do not reward a reversed axis interpretation. Proposed teaching rubric, not a reconstructed official mark scheme.
